raw_case_text:
A 55-year-old Indian gentleman with a medical history of type 2 diabetes mellitus presented with 5 days of dry cough, high-grade fever, chills, rigors, profuse sweating, and lethargy. There was no chest pain, palpitations, hemoptysis, rash, nausea, vomiting, diarrhea, or alteration in the consciousness level. He reported a history of P. vivax malaria in India 1 year back, treated successfully with artemether and lumefantrine, followed by primaquine. There was no history of recent travel, insect bites, contact with animals, or blood transfusions. Relevant history and review of systems were unremarkable.
He was febrile (39.9 degree Celsius), tachycardiac (136 beats per minute), but had no tachypnea (18 breaths per minute), a normal blood pressure (120/80 mm Hg) and was maintaining oxygen saturation of 97% on room air. Examination revealed pharyngeal and tonsillar erythema without any exudates. There was no lymphadenopathy. The chest, abdominal and neurological examinations were within normal limits. Meningeal signs were absent.
Laboratory workup revealed neutrophilic leukocytosis (Table 1). The chest X-ray was within normal limits. Considering the febrile illness and high-pretest probability for COVID-19 based on recent exposure, a nasopharyngeal swab was sent for Genexpert reverse transcriptase-polymerase chain reaction (RT-PCR) for COVID-19 and was found to be positive. A working diagnosis of mild COVID-19 upper respiratory tract infection was made. The patient was started on treatment based on the local COVID-19 management protocol at the time. 
After treatment for 3 days, there was resolution of cough and pharyngeal erythema, however, on the 4th day patient started to spike high-grade fever of 39.1 degree Celsius. Sepsis screen was ordered. The blood cultures were negative. A blood smear was done to rule out malaria. Blood smears showed ring and trophozoites of P. vivax at 0.1% (Figure 1).
Malarial treatment with Artemether/Lumefantrine four tablets twice daily was initiated. Over the next 10 days, his symptoms resolved, and he was discharged from the designated COVID-19 facility. He received the Artemether/Lumefantrine for a total of 3 days, followed by 14 days of primaquine after ruling out G6PD deficiency, and was completely asymptomatic on 6 weeks follow-up in infectious disease clinic.

subjective.chief_complaint: A 55-year-old Indian man with type 2 diabetes mellitus presented with a 5-day history of dry cough, high-grade fever, chills, rigors, profuse sweating, and lethargy.
subjective.history_of_present_illness: The patient presented with 5 days of dry cough, high fever, chills, rigors, diaphoresis, and lethargy, tested positive for COVID-19, and experienced resolution of cough and sore throat over 3 days of hospital care before spiking a recurrent high-grade fever (39.1 C) on hospital day 4.
subjective.past_medical_history: Type 2 diabetes mellitus; history of Plasmodium vivax malaria in India 1 year earlier treated with artemether-lumefantrine and primaquine; denied recent travel, insect bites, animal contact, or blood transfusions.
subjective.review_of_systems: Positive for dry cough, high-grade fever, chills, rigors, profuse sweating, and lethargy. Negative for chest pain, palpitations, hemoptysis, rash, nausea, vomiting, diarrhea, or altered consciousness.

objective.physical_examination: On admission: febrile (39.9 C), tachycardic (HR 136 bpm), RR 18 breaths/min, BP 120/80 mmHg, SpO2 97% on room air, pharyngeal and tonsillar erythema without exudates, no lymphadenopathy, and normal chest, abdominal, and neurological exams (spiked 39.1 C fever on day 4).
objective.routine_investigations: Neutrophilic leukocytosis, normal chest X-ray, normal G6PD activity, and negative bacterial blood cultures.

assessment_and_plan.assessment_and_confirmation: Final diagnosis: Long-latency relapsing Plasmodium vivax malaria co-existing with mild SARS-CoV-2 (COVID-19) upper respiratory tract infection. Confirmed by positive nasopharyngeal GeneXpert SARS-CoV-2 RT-PCR on admission and day-4 peripheral blood smear demonstrating P. vivax ring forms and trophozoites at 0.1% parasitemia. Treated with oral artemether-lumefantrine (4 tablets BID for 3 days) followed by a 14-day radical-cure course of oral primaquine (after confirming normal G6PD status), achieving complete recovery and asymptomatic status at 6-week follow-up.
